claims.text: ADR 0026 header: not built at stage-4, no multi-shop code in the repository.

The design review records moving a large shop as a trade-off point: its load and its restore are isolated, but each extra database makes migrations, backups and connections grow; deciding drivers 3 and 2; move only on ADR 0026's condition.
ADR 0026 consequence: each migration runs once more for each dedicated database; a release can leave one database behind, so migrations keep expand and contract.
Review risks table: a release leaving a dedicated database behind on migrations is owned by a backend developer; next step: expand and contract plus a job checking each database's schema version.

capacity-plan.md: each api Pod holds one Npgsql pool; Payments, Notifications, migrations and backup jobs connect to the same server; total Pods x max connections per Pod of all services must stay below max_connections, read with SHOW max_connections.

Review: each database the API reaches has its own connection pool in every Pod; rule becomes Pods x max connections per Pod x databases on one server, plus other services, below max_connections; reached first as dedicated databases grow; next step: dedicated databases on another server.
max_connections limits concurrent connections to the whole PostgreSQL 17 server, shared by all databases on it, not per database.
ADR 0026 consequence: each dedicated database has its own backup and restore; restoring that shop is restoring its database.
ADR 0026 move trigger (assumed): a shop holds more than 10% of total orders of the busiest day, or needs restoring alone by contract.

Review estimate (assumed): 10 large shops hold about 30% of orders; the largest about 10%; dedicated databases expected: a few, at most about 10; restores alone a few times a year, confirmed by the operations team.

ADR 0026: the team expects only a few dedicated databases, not hundreds; review condition: above about 10 (assumed), migration and connection cost comes close to a database per shop; a moved shop needing more isolation is ADR 0012's review condition.
Review trade-off point: restoring a shop in shared tables is slower and more manual than restoring a dedicated database; accepted because restores alone are assumed rare.
Rejected options: a database per shop, by ADR 0013, each migration running once per shop, 1,000 times; a separate deployment for a large shop, kept by ADR 0012 for contracts that demand it.
Dedicated databases at first sit on the same server as donhang: the review counts databases on one server and names moving them to another server as the next step.
Stage-4 runs 2 api Pods (deploy/gitops/config-repo-kustomize/base/api.yaml).

Expand and contract keeps each migration working with the code before it, so the version already running works on a database that has not taken the migration; the new version waits or avoids the new shape until it catches up.
claims.source_hint: backend.l4.expand-and-contract (Core concepts, How it works); ADR 0026 @ stage-4 lines 53-54

claims.text: Each dedicated database adds the same count of per-database costs whatever the shop's size: one migration run per release, one backup to restore and test, one pool in every api Pod.

A database for every shop fits when shops are tens, not a thousand, each with a contract asking for its own restore; the team then accepts tens of migration runs and spreads databases over more than one server. Monthly restores of one shop: check its move trigger.
claims.source_hint: Conditions derived from ADR 0013 rejection reason, ADR 0026 triggers and review condition (lines 63-64)

claims.text: When the server's connection slots are used up, PostgreSQL 17 refuses new ordinary connections; a few slots are kept for superusers.
Point-in-time recovery restores an entire database cluster (the whole server), not a subset of its databases.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL 17 docs, 25.3 Continuous Archiving and Point-in-Time Recovery
